items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Walter Gross walked out very artistically, and would sit down at the stool, and Tommy would lay a $20 bill on the piano... Walter Gross would reach in and put a $20 bill on the piano , before we started the Rhapsody.

ctx.x: He -- Tommy, we must say, had been on the wagon for many years, although he was known -- his doctor prescribed a certain tonic which he called it; I think it had a little

alcoholic content, but Tommy didn't drink until later on, which was one of the reasons of his death -- did the Rhapsody in Blue -- Walter tried to straighten himself out enough to play this Rhapsody, which is a feat in itself. It's a musical accomplishment.

And he would introduce Walter, and he would go into the Rhapsody, and the first thing that would happen after the introduction was Walter Gross walked out very artistically, and would sit down at the stool, and Tommy would lay a $20 bill on the piano, and the people aren't in on this inside joke, our story, and Walter Gross would reach in and put a $20 bill on the piano , before we started the Rhapsody.
